memories.memory_text: I saw Wesley Vaughn try to lift our spirits and call us to action, saying Easter was tomorrow and we should use it to get belief going again.

memories.memory_text: I said hello, good evening, ma'am—real polite—like maybe someone would answer, but they just walked past like I wasn’t even there.
A boy came running and just—went right through me. I stumbled back like I got hit, but it wasn’t the body—it was like everything inside just froze.

I zipped in fast and dropped right into the middle of the kids—felt the rush as that first snowball hit Spencer Dalton square in the back of the head. His face went from annoyed to lit up like something clicked, and I knew it was working.

I kept the chaos going—snowballs flying, kids laughing, Carson Carter and Valerie Sloane getting nailed outta nowhere. That moment when Carson Carter got hit and spun around yelling 'Spencer Dalton!'—I couldn't help but grin, knowing she had no idea it was me.
Jesse Hart poked me hard in the chest and demanded to know what my center was—like he could just dig it out of me with his finger.
He handed me that carved doll, all stern and armored, and when I opened it, there was a smaller, jollier version inside—like he was showing me some kind of secret self.

I remember crouching beside the old lantern, asking why Quinn Whitaker took the teeth, and then hearing her say they hold childhood memories—mine too. I couldn’t believe it: I had a life before I was Cameron Hayes.

I remember flying across the Westhaven Heights, feeling that surge—this was it, the key to who I was. When Jesse Hart said they’d help me get my memories back if I joined them, I didn’t hesitate. I said, 'I'm in.'
I hit it—froze that Taylor Hart right on the rooftop! Jonah Adler, did you see that? I can't believe I actually nailed it!
He said it wasn't my fight—but when he stole those teeth, he made it personal. I remember raising my staff, knowing I had to stand with them.
I closed the window and told Casey Carter we should get back.
Then I heard it — a voice laughing, calling my name... I don't know where it came from, but I swear I've heard it before.

I fell hard from the sky, slammed into that dumpster, and crumpled to the ground—everything hurt, and I could barely get the words out: 'He's stronger. I can't beat him.'
Spencer Dalton's voice cracked as he said 'I'm scared,' and it hit me like a flash—suddenly I wasn't in the alley anymore, I was back on the ice with my sister saying the exact same thing.
I looked at Spencer Dalton and said we were gonna have a little fun instead—then it hit me, clear as ice: that's it, fun isn't just what I do, it's who I am.

I nailed Quinn Whitaker with a snowball right in the face, then spotted a crate, a trash can lid, and a wok in the trash—knew we could use them to escape, and told Spencer Dalton we were going to get his friends.

I zipped through the quiet streets with Spencer Dalton, wind at my back, leaving a trail of ice behind us—then laughed as Silverline Collective tumbled after us on makeshift sleds, scared but grinning like kids.
I was gliding through the air, minding my own business, when suddenly Carson Carter turned her head and looked right at me—really saw me—for the first time, like she finally knew I was real.
I was about to step in front of Spencer Dalton to shield him, but then I felt this jolt—suddenly he was standing in front of *me*, small hand out, saying 'I will.' I froze. He was protecting *me*.

I saw Quinn Whitaker freeze in terror when the Taylor Hart turned on him. I told him, 'Looks like it's your fear they smell.'

I looked up at Westhaven Theater and thought I saw a face—just for a second—and then the old lantern came flying in, hugging me so tight I left the ground. I could feel her shaking with joy, and then Casey Carter buzzed in, making her jump back all flustered.

Jesse Hart opened the book and asked if I was ready to make it official. A stern elf hit a horn nearby. Jesse Hart asked me to vow to guard the children’s hopes, wishes, and dreams. I paused before answering.

memories.memory_text: I remember the fiery gypsy violin music as the clouds parted, revealing my fortress in the massive ice canyon — hidden, incredible, and mine.
I chiseled the final details into the ice locomotive, my eye magnified through the jeweler's tool, and chuckled as it launched into the air with wings and jets.

I was about to scold the Taylor Mercer for wrecking my train when he shouted about the Globe—I froze, then grabbed my sword and ran, heart pounding, because the Globe never alarms unless something is terribly wrong.

I saw the Globe of Belief—my lights, the children’s belief—snuffed out in waves, then swallowed by a crawling the paper notebook that came from nowhere, and when it vanished, a shadow flashed across my walls with laughter echoing behind it.
I stood atop my fortress and unleashed the Northern Light—after so many years, Silverline Collective' Call surged into the sky, and I knew they would come.
I saw the Aurora flare across the sky and knew it was time — my voice rang out, calling every Guardian to action because the children were in danger.
I sounded the emergency signal, knowing the others would hear it — we have no time to waste if the enemy has returned.
I pointed to the globe and told the others—Quinn Whitaker was here, the paper notebook all over it, and then a shadow. I saw it, I felt it in my belly, something bad is coming.
After Wesley Vaughn doubted me, I stood my ground—I know Quinn Whitaker is up to something terrible, and I called them all here for a reason. I just need to know what to do next.
I spread my arms wide and greeted him with excitement—'Hey, there he is! Cameron Hayes!'—because this moment mattered, and I wanted him to feel it, even if he didn’t understand yet.
When he complained about the sack, I laughed and claimed it proudly—'Oh, good! That was my idea!'—because he needed to see I wasn’t intimidated by his resistance.

I told Cameron Hayes to keep up as we moved through the factory—he was lagging, distracted by the Robin Warren and toys, but I had no time to waste. There was work to do, and he needed to see how things run.

I leaned in and whispered to Cameron Hayes that the Tristan Calloway don't really make the toys—we just let them believe that—then saw him glance over at the Tristan Calloway messing with ornaments and lights. It was a small truth, but one worth sharing.
I showed Cameron Hayes the magic in my workshop—the toys coming alive, the lights, the flying planes—so he could feel the wonder I carry and protect as my center.

I grabbed the reins and wrapped them tight around my arms, then called out — 'Good! Let's go! Clear!' — and cracked the reins hard. The the small case surged forward, and I felt the power beneath us, ready to fly.

As we hit the corkscrew, I glanced back and shouted, 'I hope you like the loopty loops!' — Wesley Vaughn looked green, but I couldn't help it; the thrill of the ride and his fear made it too perfect not to say.

I held up the snow globe and said, 'I say, the old lantern Palace,' and when the image appeared inside, I threw it forward and tore open a swirling portal through the sky—then shouted 'Hyah!' as I drove the the small case into the vortex.
I was pulling the the small case out of hyperdrive when these dark streaks came screaming toward us—something was terribly wrong.
I yanked the reins hard to the side, swerving through those black creatures as they tore past—had to keep everyone in the the small case from getting hit.

I saw that foul Taylor Hart skulking ahead and didn’t hesitate — I thrust the reins into Cameron Hayes’s hands and drew my sword. With one clean strike, I split it in two, and those stolen the old lantern boxes spilled out like broken promises.

The the small case was barreling toward a pillar — I barely had time to shout, 'Cameron Hayes, look out!' — then we crashed hard onto a platform. My heart pounded as I called up to the old lantern, needing to know she was still with us.
I said 'He's gone' when we landed. Then I said Quinn Whitaker would pay.

I saw the old lantern weakening, the mural crumbling—then it hit me: 'Wait, wait, wait... Idea!! HAHH!! We will collect the teeth!'—and I shouted it like a war cry, feeling the plan ignite in my chest.
I BOOMED up through the chimneys, laughing and shouting — 'A race? Is it a race??' — feeling the rush of rooftops beneath my boots and the night air crackling with energy.
Mid-leap between rooftops, I burst out of a chimney with a bang and shouted 'EPIC!!' — the word exploding into the night just like me.
We are flying over a Middle Eastern city at night in my the small case, the full Wesley Grayson above us.

I was right there at the boy's bedside, about to grab the the old lantern—easy job—when Jonah Adler just floated in and took it right from under me. That's my the old lantern! Jonah Adler! Jonah Adler!

I stood there with my bag of teeth, feeling proud—until the old lantern asked if we’d actually been leaving gifts, and I realized none of us had. My chest tightened when the others looked down, ashamed.
I climb through the window with my sack of teeth, call out to the group, and ask the old lantern how she's feeling. She says she feels believed in, and I laugh.
I placed my hand on Cameron Hayes's shoulder and told him Jonah Adler would be proud—he needed to know he belonged, even if he couldn't remember his past.

I remember the floor shaking first, then that cursed the paper notebook tearing through the factory, wrapping around the globe, and then *he* appeared—Quinn Whitaker, laughing, declaring Christmas over. My toys were falling, my Robin Warren terrified, and I could feel it—the attack wasn’t just on the workshop, but on the children.
I called out to my children as I climbed from the wreckage, but when I stood, my back gave out—I couldn't hold myself up anymore. That's when I knew it was true: my powers were gone.
Spencer Dalton said, 'It is you! I knew it wasn't a dream.' He saw me. Cameron Hayes was there too.

memories.memory_text: I reached into that sweet, glowing dream and touched the unicorn—just one finger—and watched it turn black and crumble. The way the girl flinched in her sleep... delicious.
I shaped the the paper notebook into a snarling Taylor Hart and sent it flying out the window to join the others—my army rising. The wait really is over.

I stepped out of the alley into the street, keeping clear of the moonlight, and looked up at Westhaven Theater—my old 'friend'—before declaring my Taylor Hart ready and throwing the challenge straight back at him.

I remember the screams rising from the campfire as my shadow climbed the mountain—how they trembled, how small they looked. Those were the days when fear fed me, and I stood beneath Westhaven Theater, smiling at what I had become.
I leaned in close to Silverline Collective and told them it was all about to change — their precious belief, their power, everything they stood for. The look on their faces was priceless.
I heard the crack behind me, turned, and saw the column crumbling — then told them, 'Oh look, it's happening already.' I could feel the belief slipping away, just as I planned.
I felt the Taylor Hart dissolve under my glare, its sand twisting into Jonah Adler’s shape between my fingers before I crushed it—those lights still burning on the globe, mocking me.

I cowered on the ground, looking up at Jonah Adler and Cameron Hayes, my voice trembling—'Okay, easy! You can't blame me for trying, Jonah Adler.' I let them think they'd won, that I was weak, afraid.

I stood up mid-sentence, cutting through the act—'You can have `em back!'—and as the Taylor Hart erupted from the storm drains and rooftops, I grabbed Kendall Hawthorne's mane and leaned in, grinning. 'Boo!'
I pulled myself out of the mud, cold and soaked, but I could feel it—the fear returning, and it made me smile.
I saw the bright glow of the portal close after the the small case vanished, and my Taylor Hart swarmed back to me—finally, fear was spreading again.
I saw the drawers full of baby teeth, and for a moment, all I could think about was finding my own name—just one box with 'Cameron Hayes' on it would tell me who I really was.
I spoke from the shadows, telling Cameron Hayes he was afraid of something, and I could see it in him.
I stepped out of the shadows behind Cameron Hayes and said, 'Happy Easter, Cameron Hayes,' watching his face fall as he saw the shattered eggs all around him.
I stepped forward and told Cameron Hayes I understood his loneliness — being cast out, not believed in, longing for a family — and offered him a way out of the isolation we both knew too well.
When Cameron Hayes refused, I didn't hesitate — I summoned my the paper notebook, closed in, and crushed his staff beneath my foot, leaving him broken and helpless on the ice.
I rose from the the paper notebook swirling around the globe, cackling as the Robin Warren and Tristan Calloway scattered in terror—I could feel their fear rising like smoke.
I announced they were all free to go—no more toys this year, not ever again—and the look of defeat on that Taylor Mercer’s face made it perfect.
I stood before my globe and watched the last flickers of light vanish — they were all going out, just as I planned.
I was counting them down—one by one, snapping with glee as each light died—only one stubborn flicker left, and no matter how I snapped, it refused to go out.

I felt the cold rush of Cameron Hayes's ice blast hit my sand, but it was useless—he looked shocked when I absorbed it like it was nothing. Then I charged forward and unleashed a storm of Taylor Hart that sent him crashing down, helpless.

I rode in on Kendall Hawthorne, watching them huddle around the boy like broken shields—weak, afraid, and utterly defeated. The fear in the air was thick, and I couldn't help but smile as I told them how happy I was to see them suffer.
A snowball exploded in my face—right as I was making my move—cold, sudden, undignified, and then the boy snickered, actually snickered, as if I were some joke.
I stood atop the building, smiling as my wave of the paper notebook surged through the town—finally, they would all feel the fear I commanded.
I watched in disbelief as the the paper notebook hit the children and burst into golden Dreamsand—they believed, and my Taylor Hart unraveled before my eyes.

I was savoring the chaos in the streets, smiling as my Taylor Hart did their work, when a sudden THUD made me turn—Cameron Hayes was there on the roof, already sending a streak of frost at my creations.
I was about to strike Cameron Hayes when the old lantern burst in, knocking my arrow aside—then Wesley Vaughn came roaring out of a chimney, and in an instant, my Taylor Hart disintegrated around me.
I slipped into the shadow to get away, but Jesse Hart was already leaping off the roof, scimitars in hand, cutting through the air right at me.
I rose from the ground, shaping my scythe from the paper notebook, ready to strike—but then they were all around me, knocking me down again and again.
I was just about to strike Cameron Hayes down when a golden whip coiled around my hands—Jonah Adler’s whip—and yanked me back, stopping me cold.

I was trying to escape, but then I slipped on the ice and looked up to see Jesse Hart grinning down at me—then the old lantern threw a quarter in my face and punched me, knocking out a the old lantern.
